classifications.rationale: The President directly imposes mandatory ethical duties on federal employees, including prohibitions governing their conduct; the duties apply through the order itself, although regulations will implement them.
classifications.evidence: Employees shall not hold financial interests that conflict with the conscientious performance of duty.

classifications.rationale: This segment inseparably combines immediate employee duties and an outside-income prohibition with directions requiring the Office of Government Ethics to promulgate legally operative standards and disclosure regulations later, plus internal manual preparation.
classifications.evidence: No employee who is appointed by the President to a full-time noncareer position in the executive branch (including full-time noncareer employees in the White House Office, the Office of Policy Development, and the Office of Cabinet Affairs), shall receive any earned income for any outside employment or activity performed during that Presidential appointment.

classifications.rationale: This segment inseparably combines a present statutory treatment of EOP components, mandated later regulations and agency measures, discretionary coordination and administration, and delegations of presidential authority.
classifications.evidence: those agencies shall be treated as one agency under section 207(c) of title 18, United States Code.

classifications.rationale: This segment inseparably combines internal revocation of prior executive orders with savings clauses that presently preserve existing actions, authorize performance of specified preexisting contracts, and continue confidentiality protections.
classifications.evidence: employees may carry out preexisting contractual obligations entered into before April 12, 1989.
